274	    /// `read` → `plan` → `edit` over the document's current handle: the edit and the summary's
275	    /// text, or the refusals one per line.
276	    private func planned(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> (SpeakerSwitch.Edit?, String) {
277	        guard let input = SpeakerSwitch.read(
278	            from: document, clips: nil, pairing: chosenPairing, range: nil, settings: settings)
279	        else {
280	            return (nil, "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment.")
281	        }
282	        switch SpeakerSwitch.plan(input) {
283	        case .refused(let reasons):
284	            return (nil, reasons.joined(separator: "\n"))
285	        case .planned(let shots, let added):
286	            let container = document.editedProject
287	            let replacing = writePopup.numberOfItems > 0 ? track(of: writePopup) : nil
288	            if let replacing, let why = SpeakerSwitch.replaceRefusal(
289	                replacing, input: input, selection: document.selection, in: container.snapshot)
290	            {
291	                return (nil, why)
292	            }
293	            do {
294	                switch try SpeakerSwitch.edit(
295	                    shots, input: input, muteCameras: muteBox.state == .on, replacing: replacing,
296	                    selection: document.selection, in: container)
297	                {
298	                case .edit(let edit):
299	                    return (edit, SpeakerSwitch.summary(shots, added: added, names: names))
300	                case .refused(let why):
301	                    return (nil, why)
302	                }
303	            } catch {
304	                return (nil, error.localizedDescription)
305	            }
306	        }
307	    }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

274	    /// `read` → `plan` → `edit` over the document's current handle: the edit and the summary's
275	    /// text, or the refusals one per line.
276	    private func planned(_ document: ProjectDocument) -> (SpeakerSwitch.Edit?, String) {
277	        guard let input = SpeakerSwitch.read(
278	            from: document, clips: nil, pairing: chosenPairing, range: nil, settings: settings)
279	        else {
280	            return (nil, "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment.")
281	        }
282	        switch SpeakerSwitch.plan(input) {
283	        case .refused(let reasons):
284	            return (nil, reasons.joined(separator: "\n"))
285	        case .planned(let shots, let added):
286	            let container = document.editedProject
287	            let replacing = writePopup.numberOfItems > 0 ? track(of: writePopup) : nil
288	            if let replacing, let why = SpeakerSwitch.replaceRefusal(
289	                replacing, input: input, selection: document.selection, in: container.snapshot)
290	            {
291	                return (nil, why)
292	            }
293	            do {
294	                switch try SpeakerSwitch.edit(
295	                    shots, input: input, muteCameras: muteBox.state == .on, replacing: replacing,
296	                    selection: document.selection, in: container)
297	                {
298	                case .edit(let edit):
299	                    return (edit, SpeakerSwitch.summary(shots, added: added, names: names))
300	                case .refused(let why):
301	                    return (nil, why)
302	                }
303	            } catch {
304	                return (nil, error.localizedDescription)
305	            }
306	        }
307	    }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the

  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map

  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,

  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a

  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`

  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an

  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`

  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:

  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not

  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`

  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

import AppKit

/// The Analyzing sheet (spec §11 CJ-28; road map "creator-jobs" CJ2b): up
/// while the analysis a menu command plans with is made on this Mac, one row
/// per media whose request missed the cache — its file name, a determinate
/// bar, and "Waiting" until the job's first frame, then "NN %", then "Done".
/// The first command is Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes (CJ-29); any kind whose
/// result a command plans with comes through here (CO-6 amends it for a
/// render-substituted kind). A tool call shows no sheet and waits.
///
/// **One owner.** The sheet wants every row's request under one lane owner
/// (alive while the document is open; `settled` tells the document its
/// package changed) when it appears, and releases it in `viewDidDisappear` —
/// its ONE release, on every exit: Stop, landing, failure, the window
/// closing. A disappearance with no outcome and no Stop (the window ordered
/// out, as a minimize does) clears `didStart`, so the next `viewDidAppear`
/// wants again what has not landed and restarts the poll. What a job already
/// published stays cached (CJ-21).
///
/// **Polled, not told:** a 0.1 s `Timer` in the `.common` modes reads
/// `AnalysisLane.progress(of:)` and `run(of:)`. When every run has landed, or
/// one failed, the sheet keeps the outcome and dismisses itself; `finished`
/// is called once, on the main queue's next turn after `viewDidDisappear`
/// (`AudioSyncSheetController`'s reason: the window still reports the sheet
/// attached while it disappears). Stop only dismisses and calls nothing, so
/// no edit lands. While the sheet is attached every editor action validates
/// false (`EditorViewController.validateUserInterfaceItem`).
final class AnalyzingSheetController: NSViewController {
    struct Row {
        let name: String
        let request: AnalysisRequest
    }

    enum Outcome {
        case landed
        case failed(name: String, why: String)
    }

    static let pollInterval: TimeInterval = 0.1

    private let document: ProjectDocument
    private let command: String
    private let rows: [Row]
    private let finished: (Outcome) -> Void
    private let lane = AnalysisLane.shared
    private let owner: Int

    private var bars: [NSProgressIndicator] = []
    private var statuses: [NSTextField] = []
    /// Set in `loadView`; implicitly unwrapped for exactly that reason
    /// (app/CLAUDE.md).
    private var stopButton: NSButton!
    private var hiddenButton: NSButton!

    private var timer: Timer?
    private var didStart = false
    private var reappearing = false
    private var answered = false
    private var stopped = false
    private var outcome: Outcome?

    init(
        document: ProjectDocument, command: String, rows: [Row],
        finished: @escaping (Outcome) -> Void
    ) {
        self.document = document
        self.command = command
        self.rows = rows
        self.finished = finished
        owner = AnalysisLane.shared.newOwner()
        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
    }

    @available(*, unavailable)
    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
        fatalError("AnalyzingSheetController does not support NSCoder")
    }

    override func loadView() {
        var views: [NSView] = []

---
title: "Set up several cameras"
description: Put each camera on its own track, line them up by their sound, name them, and get a program track ready for a show filmed with more than one camera.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Set up a show filmed with several cameras, such as a podcast with a camera on each guest or an interview with a wide and a close shot, so you can cut between them.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio', 'Track ▸ New Track', 'Clip ▸ Split']}
  keys={['⇧⌘N', '⌘T']}
  tools={['sync_audio', 'copy_pieces']}
/>

## How multicam works

There's no special multicam clip. Each camera is an ordinary clip on an ordinary track, and the edit you watch is a **program track** in front of them, made of pieces of whichever camera you want at each moment.

<Steps>

1. Put [one camera on each track](#one-camera-per-track) and line them up.
2. [Name the tracks](#name-the-tracks) after their cameras.
3. Build [the program track](#the-program-track), by hand or with [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
4. Fix single shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

</Steps>

## One camera per track

Put each camera's recording on a track of its own, then line the recordings up in time. **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** does this from their sound: select the recordings and choose it. See [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).

If a camera stopped and started again, its pieces can all sit on the one track.

## Name the tracks

Double-click a track's header and type the camera's name. These names are what **Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸** lists, and what the Switch by Speaker sheet uses for its cameras and microphones.

When two listed tracks share a name, Frame Job adds each one's position counted from the back, for example "Camera (2)" and "Camera (3)".

## The program track

Choose **Track ▸ New Track** (<kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>). The new track lands in front of the others, which is where the program goes.

[Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) can write the whole program track for you, and it adds its own track, so skip this step if you're using it.

To build the program by hand:

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the start of a camera's clip.
2. Select the clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>, then <kbd>⌘V</kbd>. The copy lands on the front track at the playhead, in sync with the camera.
3. Select the copy, move the playhead to a cut and choose **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). Repeat for each cut.
4. Select a shot and pick another camera from [**Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸**](/multicam/switch-angle/).

</Steps>

A pasted copy keeps its sound on, so the same sound plays from the program track and the camera's track until you [mute one of them](/audio/mute-and-solo/). The pieces Switch by Speaker writes have their sound off.

An agent builds the program with one `copy_pieces` call per camera. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).

## Shown or hidden

The camera tracks stay underneath the program. Leave them shown and the program track, being in front, covers them. Or hide them with the hide switch in the track header, or **Hide Video** in the header's right-click menu. See [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).

Either way they still work as cameras: a hidden track's clips are still listed by Switch Angle and still count for Switch by Speaker.

## Microphones

Switch by Speaker needs to know which recording hears which person. It works this out from what you've selected.

| Selected | What counts as a microphone |
| --- | --- |
| Clips with their sound on and no picture, such as a recorder or a separate microphone file | Every track holding one |
| No clips like that | Each camera that plays sound is its own microphone |
| A camera's sound split off with **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** | Never chosen for you, but you can pick it in a **Microphone** pop-up |

So keep each person's microphone file on a track of its own, beside the cameras, and select it with them. Only the selected clips on a microphone's track are listened to.

The sheet's **Microphone** pop-ups list every track holding a selected clip with its sound on, so you can swap in a detached camera sound or a camera's own sound there. An agent can name a detached camera sound as a microphone too.

When the selection comes to exactly one microphone and two or more cameras, Switch by Speaker can't tell people apart by ear, so it decides from their faces. That includes the case where only one camera has sound. See [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/).

## Related

- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/)
- [Add, rename and reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/)

---
title: "Switch by Speaker"
description: Cut a whole Program track from a conversation, showing whoever is talking on each microphone, as one undo step.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Switch by Speaker cuts a whole program for you from a conversation. It listens to each person's microphone and writes a new track that shows whoever is talking.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
  tools="switch_by_speaker"
  needs="Nothing. It reads each microphone's loudness and speech detection, made on your Mac at import, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Switch by Speaker

<Steps>

1. [Synchronize the recordings](#synchronize-first) with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.

2. Select every camera's clips and every microphone's clips. <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking a track header selects all the clips on that track.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it sits right after Synchronize Audio in the **Clip** menu.

  alt="The Switch by Speaker sheet. Two speaker rows pair the Camera microphone with the Camera track and the Screen microphone with the Screen track. - the selection holds clips with a picture on two or more tracks, each of which is a camera

- no sheet is open on the window

The cut covers the [In–Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) when one is set, otherwise the whole length of the selected camera clips.

| The summary says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "The microphone on track … is still being analysed…" | Frame Job hasn't finished measuring that file's loudness or detecting its speech, which often happens straight after an import. Try again in a moment. |
| "The microphone on track … has no speech between … and …, so it never says who is talking." | That microphone hears no speech in the range. Check you've paired the right track, or shorten the range. |
| "No angle has a picture between … and …." | No camera covers that stretch of the range. Set an In–Out range that avoids it, or fill the gap. |
| "The speaker on track … has no microphone." | A row has no microphone that's selected and sounding. |
| "The microphone on track … has no angle to show its speaker." | A row has no camera. |
| "Track … is the microphone for 2 speakers; each person needs their own microphone." | One microphone is on two rows. See [Good to know](#good-to-know) for when that's allowed. |
| "Switch by Speaker takes at most nine angles…" | More than nine tracks hold a selected picture. Select fewer. |

| "The project's audio plan could not be read. Try again in a moment." | Frame Job couldn't read the project's sound just then. |

- Silence holds the current shot, and so does a reply under a second long.
- A pause under half a second between one person's words doesn't end their turn.

- When two people talk at once, [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.

A camera clip still linked to its detached sound can't be switched. The sheet says so and names the clip, ending "Attach Audio first". Choose [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) to put the two back together, then try again.

Only a linked camera clip crossing the range stops the cut.

**Switch** writes all of this as one undo step, **Switch by Speaker**. The selection stays. A selected clip cut at the range's ends brings its new half into the selection.

Switch adds a track named **Program** directly in front of the front-most camera. It holds a piece of the chosen camera for each shot, in sync, with the picture on and the sound off.

To write over an earlier Program track instead, use [**Write to**](/multicam/switch-settings/#write-to).

### Cameras hidden

Switch hides the camera tracks so only the program shows.

A camera track that holds anything outside the range isn't hidden. Its clips are cut at the range's ends and their pictures are switched off inside the range only.

Nothing outside the range changes. The microphones aren't edited, so what you hear stays the same, apart from any camera sound you chose to [mute](/multicam/switch-settings/#mute-the-cameras-own-sound).

- The microphones are heard through the mix's own channels, so a clip's sound settings count.
- Switch by Speaker doesn't remember your pairing. The speaker rows open fresh each time.

## With an agent

`switch_by_speaker` takes the sheet's values and a few it doesn't show. An agent can name the range directly, ahead of the In–Out range, and pair people by hand. It can also ask for the shots without editing anything, and set the shortest turn that cuts and how far one microphone must lead to count alone. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/) and [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/).

- [Set up several cameras](/multicam/set-up/)
- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)

---
title: "Switch by Speaker settings"
description: What each row of the Switch by Speaker sheet does, its default and range, and which values Frame Job remembers.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These rows of the [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) sheet shape the cut: where it opens, how long shots last, and how it treats two people talking at once.

<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…" tools="switch_by_speaker" />

| Row | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [**Wide:**](#wide) | The camera that opens the cut and breaks in | The one camera no person uses, otherwise None | Any camera, or None |
| [**Minimum shot:**](#minimum-shot) | The shortest shot allowed | 2 s (3 s with [one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)) | 0.5 to 30 s |
| [**Cut:**](#cut-before-speech) | How long before speech the cut comes | 0.2 s | 0 to 1 s |
| [**Crosstalk:**](#crosstalk-shows) | What shows while two people talk at once | Wide | Wide, Current speaker |
| [**Ignore bleed:**](#ignore-bleed) | How far below a speaker's level a voice is ignored | 15 dB | 3 to 40 dB |
| [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after) | Breaks up a long monologue | Off | 2 to 600 s |
| [**Mute the cameras' own sound**](#mute-the-cameras-own-sound) | Turns the cameras' sound off inside the range | On when no microphone is on a camera track | |
| [**Write to:**](#write-to) | Where the cut goes | A new Program track | |

The number fields take up to two decimal places.

## Wide

The camera for your wide shot. Choose any of the cameras, or **None**. If exactly one camera is left over once every person has theirs, it's picked to start with. Otherwise the row opens on **None**.

The Wide shows:

- at the start of the cut
- during crosstalk, when [**Crosstalk**](#crosstalk-shows) shows **Wide**
- after [**Cut to the wide after**](#cut-to-the-wide-after)
- for a stretch where another camera has nothing to show

When nobody is talking, the current shot holds. It doesn't go to the Wide.

## Minimum shot

The shortest shot the cut may have, from 0.5 to 30 s. The default is 2 s.

A shorter shot merges into the shot before it when that camera covers the stretch, otherwise into the shot after it. A short shot that neither neighbour covers stays.

Raising this is also the way out when the cut would add more clips than a project can hold.

## Cut before speech

The **Cut:** row sets how long before a new speaker's first word the cut comes, from 0 to 1 s. The default is 0.2 s, and the cut lands on a whole frame.

## Late cuts under heavy bleed

With heavy bleed in a noisy room, a cut can land later than **Cut** asks. With another voice 24 dB down under −45 dBFS of noise, the worst case measured was about 35 ms before the first word instead of 0.2 s.

## Crosstalk shows

What the program shows while two people talk at once for a second or more. **Wide** cuts to the [Wide](#wide), and **Current speaker** holds the shot you're on. With no Wide chosen, crosstalk holds the current shot whatever this says.

Crosstalk shorter than a second starts nothing. A stretch under half a second between two bursts of crosstalk counts as crosstalk.

Two microphones are crosstalk when both hear a voice above their [bleed](#ignore-bleed) line. If one leads the other by 8 dB or more, measured against each one's own speaker, it counts alone.

## Ignore bleed

Every microphone also hears the other people, quieter. A voice more than this far below a microphone's own speaker is bleed, and never counts as that person talking. It runs from 3 to 40 dB, and the default is 15 dB.

- Raise it if a quiet guest is never shown.
- Lower it if someone is shown while only the other person talks.

A voice must also stand 6 dB above the microphone's quiet background to count. This row doesn't appear in the [one-microphone sheet](/multicam/one-microphone/#the-sheet-in-this-mode).

## Cut to the wide after

Breaks up a long monologue. Tick the box and set how long one person may hold the screen, from 2 to 600 s. It's off by default, and the field offers 20 s.

When a shot reaches that length, the Wide shows for one [**Minimum shot**](#minimum-shot), then the speaker's camera returns. This repeats to the end of the shot.

It needs a Wide. With **Wide** on **None**, ticking it does nothing.

## Mute the cameras' own sound

Switches the cameras' scratch sound off inside the range. It's ticked to start with when no microphone is on a camera track, which is when the microphones are separate recordings.

It never touches a microphone's track, so a camera used as a microphone keeps its sound.

## Write to

Writes the new cut over an earlier Program track instead of adding another. Choose **Replace the shots on** and the track's name, or leave it on **A new Program track**, the default.

The row shows only when an earlier track can be replaced. That track must:

- be unlocked
- hold no selected clip
- sit in front of the cameras
- have something in the range
- hold only pieces of the cameras there

The track is cleared over the range and cut at its ends. Nothing on it outside the range changes.

## Remembered values

**Minimum shot**, **Cut**, **Crosstalk** and **Ignore bleed** are kept for the next time. They're written only when you change a value and press **Switch**, so **Cancel** keeps the old ones.

**Minimum shot** isn't remembered in the one-microphone sheet. Every other row opens fresh each time. An agent's call reads none of the remembered values and uses the defaults in the table above.

## Related

- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/)
- [Tools: multicam](/mcp/tools-multicam/)

---
title: "Cut from faces with one microphone"
description: When one microphone hears everyone, let Switch by Speaker decide who is talking from the cameras' pictures, and check the result.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When one microphone hears everyone, it can't say who's talking. [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) then decides from the cameras' pictures instead, by watching whose mouth is moving.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…"
  tools="switch_by_speaker"
  needs="Nothing. Face detection and speech detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## One microphone for everyone

Frame Job works this way when your selection holds exactly one microphone and two or more cameras. That includes a selection where only one camera has sound. See [Microphones](/multicam/set-up/#microphones).

<Steps>

1. Line the recordings up with **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**.

2. Select the cameras' clips and the microphone's clip, then choose **Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**.

3. If the cameras haven't been read yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#finding-faces-first).

4. Check [the sheet](#the-sheet-in-this-mode) and choose **Switch**.

5. [Look through the result](#faces-only-guess) and fix any wrong shots.

</Steps>

While the microphone hears speech, the camera whose person's mouth moves most is shown:

- Each camera's person is the largest face in its picture.
- Frame Job watches that mouth opening and closing over half a second.
- A camera wins when its mouth moves at least half as much again as the next camera's (1.5×) and above a small floor.
- When two mouths move alike it's crosstalk, and [**Crosstalk**](/multicam/switch-settings/#crosstalk-shows) decides what shows.
- With no speech, or no mouth to read, the current shot holds.

The rest of the cut works as it does with several microphones, and it writes the same [Program track](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/#the-program-track) as one undo step.

## Finding faces first

Frame Job reads faces from its [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of each camera. When a camera's faces haven't been found yet, an **Analyzing** sheet comes up first, with a bar for each file. The Switch by Speaker sheet opens once they're found.

Only the part of each camera the range needs is analysed, and what's found is kept in the project's cache, so next time it's quicker or skipped.

| If | Then |
| --- | --- |
| You choose **Stop** | Everything stays as it was, and what was found so far is kept. Choose the command again to carry on. |
| The analysis fails | Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
| The project changed while it analysed | Frame Job beeps, says so at the foot of the inspector, and switches nothing. Choose the command again. |

## The sheet in this mode

The sheet changes to suit one microphone:

- One **Microphone:** pop-up replaces the speaker rows, and **Cameras:** lists every camera.
- There's no **Ignore bleed** row, because there's no second microphone to bleed into.
- **Minimum shot** opens at 3 s, not 2 s, and isn't remembered.
- **Wide** opens on **None**.

The other rows work as they do in [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/).

A camera with no face whose mouth can be read stops the cut. The summary reads "The camera on track … shows no face whose mouth can be read between … and …, so it never says who is talking." A camera whose faces still aren't found reads "The camera on track … is still being analysed — its faces have not been found yet."

## Wide in this mode

Choose a **Wide** to show it during crosstalk. That camera then takes no part in deciding who talks, so a true wide shot whose faces are too small to read won't stop the cut. With no Wide, crosstalk holds the current shot.

With only two cameras, making one the Wide leaves a single camera for faces to decide between. Faces no longer decide and the warning leaves the summary. The other camera then shows whenever the microphone hears speech.

## Faces only guess

The summary starts "Faces guess who is talking; check the cuts."

Mouths that move without speaking, such as laughing, chewing or a hand over the mouth, can put a cut in the wrong place. So can a face turned away. Look through the result and fix those shots with [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/).

## Good to know

- Only the largest face in a camera is read. With two people in one shot, the other person's mouth doesn't count.
- Only video files are read for faces. A still picture on a camera track has no mouth to read.
- Pointing every speaker row at one microphone in the ordinary sheet also reads faces. It doesn't bring up the Analyzing sheet, so a camera not yet read stays "still being analysed". To find its faces, select only the one microphone and the cameras, and choose the command again.

## With an agent

There's no Analyzing sheet for `switch_by_speaker`. The call waits up to 60 seconds for the faces, then stops with what it found kept, and calling it again carries on. Its answer says which way it decided and repeats the warning. See [Copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/).

## Related

- [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/)
- [Switch by Speaker settings](/multicam/switch-settings/)
- [Switch Angle](/multicam/switch-angle/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
